review_scope: Read current immutable source only; no browser, PostHog state query/config change, replay start, model call or test run.

findings.fact: normalSession is ordinary auth /api/auth/get-session, not PostHog. The final submit gate checks fresh browser, login/workspace/profile, official backend response and source revision; no PostHog, Replay, recording or analytics-session check exists.

SDK init is conditional on posthogConfig.token. Local config opts into recording availability (disable_session_recording:false), sampleRate:1, input/text/attribute masking, blocked sensitive media/contenteditable, headers/body/console disabled. The loaded callback only registers safe properties and a capture sink; it publishes no readiness proof.

Replay URL/request metadata is sanitized; $snapshot explicitly survives with only token/distinct/session/window/lib/snapshot keys. Other events use a narrow allowlist. This path does not contain a consent or Replay feature-flag gate.

Public build token comes from NEXT_PUBLIC_POSTHOG_KEY with empty-string fallback. Ingestion host chooses POSTHOG_HOST, then NEXT_PUBLIC_POSTHOG_HOST, then US default. Presence/correct deployment values were not queried.
PostHogAnalytics mounts only when posthogConfig.token is truthy; no consent UI or Replay feature flag wraps it in this layout.

Waits for auth resolution, handles reset/identify, tags smoke accounts test_account:true, sends sanitized pageview and reloads flags. No Replay-specific feature-flag gate or smoke-account exclusion appears in this Web path.

A separate SDK-independent desktop/phone analytics helper has enabled opt-in/out control. The inspected Web bootstrap/layout/component does not import this helper; it is not evidence of a consent gate in this real browser actor's path.
Web posthog-js dependency is pinned to 1.438.13; exact runtime/public API behavior was not inferred from an uninspected SDK implementation.

narrow_recommendation: Add one bounded, fail-closed readiness condition immediately before the existing single paid Create task click.

Use the real browser's initialized SDK/current session and actual recording-start state; if a small bridge is needed, expose only a read-only safe status and actual session identity from the existing client callback. Do not inject storage/IDs, opt in, force-start recording, or assume an ESM SDK is available as window.posthog.

Require a genuine recording-start observation and, where available through closed metadata, a successful snapshot transport acknowledgement for the same current session. Never treat merely allocating/reading an ID or a pageview as Replay-start proof; do not inspect snapshot payload.

Record only closed readiness booleans, actual opaque session ID, bounded timestamps and a closed failure code. Unavailable/unready/unknown must abort before submitClicks becomes 1 and use existing cleanup.
Keep the scope to this actor/client readiness seam; no consent framework, project configuration change, generalized browser framework or historical replay fabrication is proposed.
remaining_limits: Source config is not evidence that the production key, SDK script, remote recording policy or upload transport is currently functioning.
A startup/transport receipt still does not prove native playback or masking; final Replay visual verification remains required.
No actual PostHog session ID was fetched, synthesized or copied in this review.
